description: The JERICHO-E-usage repository contains the Python and Jupyter workflow for compiling hourly useful-energy profiles for Germany's 38 NUTS-2 regions. Its research team separates four consuming sectors and eight energy-service categories, allowing the generated profiles to support coupled infrastructure models. GitHub provides a notebook, required input material and a Conda environment specification under the MIT licence. The related Figshare archived-code deposit instead states CC0; that label is retained as an archive-specific statement. Both are freely accessible. The workflow can prepare regional heat, electricity and mobility service-demand inputs alongside data-when2heat-heat-demand-heat-pump-cop. A caveat is that resulting useful-energy profiles depend on the supplied statistics and allocation assumptions, and they are not direct measurements of final energy purchases. The inspected own documentation establishes hourly resolution but does not verify every calendar convention or input reference year. The notebook and environment were not executed, and compatibility with current Python packages remains unchecked.
